results.claim: Reachability is exactly a sparse unary congruence-closure query.
results.proof_sketch: Write a dual edge as (o,X,t), suppressing its pin. Let θ be the least equivalence on wires such that t θ t' and edges (o,X,t),(o',X,t') imply o θ o'. A path that begins and ends above the same stack suffix has a well-nested push/pop word. Induction on its decomposition into concatenations and outermost push-X/balanced/pop-X segments shows that its endpoints are θ-equivalent. Conversely, a folding step is realized by pushing X along its first cited edge, following the already-realized stack-neutral path between the targets, and popping X along the reverse of the second edge; reflexivity, reversal, and concatenation realize equivalence closure. Thus θ is exactly bottom-stack-neutral reachability. The DPDA exits precisely from an outer-pin wire while the bottom symbol remains, so exitability is equivalent to the start being θ-equivalent to an outer-pin wire. In the quotient, each box X induces the well-defined partial unary map [t]↦[o].

results.claim: There is a deterministic O(B+(W+E) log(W+E))-time, O(W+E+B)-space algorithm, eliminating the dense W·B initialization.
results.proof_sketch:
For every current target class C, maintain a map D_C whose key X stores one original edge (o,X,t) with t∈C. Radix-sort the initial edges by (t,X), retain one representative per key, and queue the origins of duplicates. Whenever a queued pair belongs to different wire classes, merge those classes and meld their maps. A common key queues the two stored origins and deletes one representative. At enqueue time the cited targets are already equivalent, so every queued origin equality is forced by θ and remains forced as classes grow. At termination, every pair of same-box edges with equivalent targets has equivalent origins, so the partition is stable. Crucially, stability alone is not being identified with leastness: forced merges give the computed partition P⊆θ, while terminal stability and minimality of θ give θ⊆P.

There is at most one collision event per deleted original edge, hence at most E. Smaller-to-larger member relabeling costs O(W log W). Deterministic split/join balanced trees meld maps of sizes m≤n in O(m log(n/m+1)); charges to surviving entries telescope with map growth, while an overlapping entry is deleted once, for O(E log(E+1)) total. Initial bounded-integer radix sorting costs O(W+E+B), and all lists, maps, edges, and queue records occupy O(W+E+B) space.

results.claim: Both outcomes have certificates of size O(W+E) verifiable deterministically in O(W+E+B) time.
results.proof_sketch:
For a negative certificate, supply a bounded class number P(v) for every wire. Radix-sort edges by (X,P(t)) and verify that each group has a unique value P(o). Equality of class numbers is automatically an equivalence, and the group test makes it stable. P need not be the least closure: the least θ refines every stable P, so separation of the start from every outer-pin wire in P implies separation in θ. Conversely, θ itself supplies a certificate for every negative instance.

For a positive certificate, supply a chronological binary merge forest with at most W−1 internal nodes. Each internal node cites two earlier child components, two original edges with the same box, and an earlier node q; their origins must lie in the respective child subtrees and both targets below q. Chronology makes induction sound: q certifies target equivalence, so the folding rule certifies the new component. Unique parent links establish a forest, and one DFS gives intervals for constant-time containment tests. A root containing the start and an outer-pin wire certifies exit. Recording any successful sequence of forced class merges produces such a forest, proving completeness. Certificate and verifier storage are linear.

results.claim: The target O(W+E+B) bound holds for graded dual graphs: graphs admitting an integer rank ρ with ρ(o)=ρ(t)+1 for every edge (o,X,t).
results.proof_sketch:
Induction on folding steps shows that equivalences never cross ranks. Process ranks increasingly. After rank r−1 is final, group edges with rank-r origins by (X,class(t)); add a star among the origins of each group and compute ordinary connected components on rank-r wires. These components are exactly the final rank-r classes: all currently forced merges are included, and every rule capable of merging rank-r origins depends only on rank-(r−1) target classes, which no later rank can change. Timestamp arrays of lengths B and W implement sparse grouping, and the stars contain at most E edges overall, so every edge and wire is processed O(1) times.

If ρ is not supplied, view each edge as the constraint ρ(o)−ρ(t)=1. DFS on each weak component assigns and checks these integer potentials in O(W+E) time. Componentwise normalization yields ranks in a range of length O(W), permitting linear bucket ordering. Total time and space are O(W+E+B).

results.claim: Canonical longest-path box stratification is recognizable in O(W+E+B) time and includes non-graded instances with nontrivial folds.
results.proof_sketch: Reverse every dual edge (o,X,t) to a feature arc t→X o. Topological sorting either finds a cycle or computes λ(v), the maximum number of arcs on a directed path ending at v; 0≤λ(v)<W. Call the acyclic graph box-stratified when, for every box X and level s, all X-arcs with tail level s have heads at one common level. Bucket arcs by tail level. While scanning one level, timestamped arrays indexed by the B boxes record the first head level and compare all later occurrences, so recognition takes O(W+E+B) time and space. The class is genuinely non-graded and folding is not vacuous: arcs a→P b, b→Q d, a→R c, c→S e, a→X d, a→X e have levels 0,1,1,2,2, and the two X-arcs force d≡e. Yet unit-difference grading would give ρ(d)=ρ(a)+2 along a→b→d and ρ(d)=ρ(a)+1 along a→d, a contradiction. Distinct pins realize all six arcs as a valid dual maze.

results.claim: In a box-stratified feature DAG, every class of the least folding equivalence θ is homogeneous in canonical level λ.
results.proof_sketch: Start from the identity relation, whose classes are homogeneous. Equivalence closure of pairs joining equal levels preserves homogeneity. For the only additional rule, suppose same-box arcs t→X o and t'→X o' have equivalent tails. By the induction invariant λ(t)=λ(t')=s. Box stratification says all X-arcs leaving level s have one head level, hence λ(o)=λ(o'). Thus every forced pair also joins equal levels. Induction through any finite construction of the least fixed point proves the invariant for θ. In particular, because λ strictly increases along every feature arc, a fold whose origins have level r depends only on equivalence information at levels below r.

results.claim: A level-by-level star decomposition computes θ, and hence exit reachability, in O(W+E+B) time and space on box-stratified feature DAGs.
results.proof_sketch: Process levels increasingly. At level r, all target classes of arcs whose origins have level r are already final. For every pair (X,target class), add a star among its level-r origins, and assign the connected components of the resulting undirected graph as the level-r classes. Every star edge is a forced fold, so the computed relation P is contained in θ. Conversely, the final P is stable: if same-box arcs have P-equivalent targets, level homogeneity gives those targets one lower level; their class was final when their common origin level was processed, so the two origins occur in one star group and are P-equivalent. Minimality of θ gives θ⊆P, hence equality. Per-level wire and edge buckets cost O(W+E); timestamped arrays of lengths B and W group touched boxes and target classes without dense W·B initialization; a k-edge group contributes only k−1 star edges, so all component searches cost O(W+E). The reachability characterization above then transfers θ to the exit query, proving the stated time and space bounds.

results.claim: Repeated global fixed-point rescanning can require Θ(W) changing rounds even with one box and E=Θ(W).
results.proof_sketch: For n≥0, use wires z,a_0,b_0,…,a_n,b_n and one box X. Add edges a_0→X z and b_0→X z; for 1≤k≤n add a_k→X a_{k−1} and b_k→X b_{k−1}. Starting with singleton classes, synchronous round 1 merges only a_0 with b_0, and round k+1 merges only a_k with b_k. Induction shows that z and different levels never merge. Hence there are exactly n+1 changing rounds, while W=2n+3 and E=2n+2. Conversely, each changing round strictly reduces the number of classes, so there are at most W−1 such rounds. This proves Θ(W). Distinct pins can label all edges, so the family is a valid one-box dual-maze representation. The result limits global rescanning, not all possible algorithms.

results.claim: Any folding implementation that explicitly stores every live box representative per class and handles each class union by scanning all representatives of one operand has an Ω((W+E+B) log(W+E+B)) worst case.
results.proof_sketch:
Let N=2^h. On data wires v_0,…,v_{N−1}, prescribe the balanced bottom-up union list: adjacent pairs, then adjacent 2-blocks, and so on. Give the first pair two same-box edges to a common target. For every later listed pair, give its origins two edges of a fresh box whose targets are the endpoints of the preceding listed pair. Thus only the first union is initially enabled, each union enables exactly its successor, and scheduling cannot avoid N/2^{k+1} unions of two classes containing 2^k data wires at level k.

For each i add two Y_i-edges, one targeting v_i and one targeting a separate anchor a_i. After the balanced root union, a fresh rule merges a_0 into it; the resulting Y_0 collision merges controls p_0,q_0, which enables a_1, then Y_1, and so on. The final control equality alone merges the non-outer start with v_0. Hence every Y_i occurs twice and is load-bearing for the positive query, yet throughout the balanced phase each k-wire data class contains k distinct live Y-representatives. Scanning either operand at a level-k union therefore costs at least 2^k, totaling (N/2)h representative inspections. Assign distinct pins to all edges. The family has W=4N+2, E=6N, and B=3N, so its input size is Θ(N). This is a lower bound only for eager whole-operand melding, not for arbitrary algorithms; a linear solution must use a lazier/shared organization or a different idea.

results.claim: The bounded-key radix sorts used above rely only on the standard lexicographic stable-pass invariant, not on preservation of earlier-key blocks.
results.proof_sketch: For records (a,b), first stably counting-sort on b and then stably counting-sort on a. The final pass orders distinct a-values, and within each equal-a group its stability preserves the already nondecreasing b-order; hence the result is lexicographically sorted by (a,b). The second pass may interleave the b-blocks created by the first, and no contrary invariant is used. Thus sorting (t,X) uses passes X then t, and sorting (X,P(t)) uses passes P(t) then X. Since the coordinate ranges are respectively bounded by W and B and there are E records, these sorts take O(W+E+B) time and space.

final_writeup:
The independent audit contains no REFUTED or UNRESOLVED item: all seven parent claims are VERIFIED and are retained. Its target-coverage judgment also remains correct. The source asks for an unrestricted deterministic O(W+E+B)-time exit-reachability algorithm in the source representation. The general constructor here still has a logarithmic factor; linear certificate verification is not a linear certificate-finding algorithm; and both linear constructions below require structural restrictions. The eager-melding lower bound is not a lower bound against all algorithms. The strongest justified claimed_resolution therefore remains PARTIAL.

For a dual edge (o,X,t), let θ be the least equivalence for which equivalent targets of same-box edges force equivalent origins. Protected-stack paths are reversible and composable. Decomposing a bottom-neutral instruction word into concatenations and push-X/balanced/pop-X excursions gives one inclusion in θ; realizing each fold by a push, an already realized neutral target path, and the reverse pop gives the other. Hence θ is exactly stack-neutral wire reachability, and an exit is reachable exactly when the start class contains an outer-pin wire. Equivalently, reversing each dual edge gives a sparse feature graph t→X o, and θ is its least quotient in which every feature X is single-valued.

The general deterministic algorithm stores for each current target class only boxes represented by incoming edges. A same-box collision queues the two origins and deletes one representative. Every queued merge is forced; every representative is deleted at most once; and quiescence makes the final partition stable. Forcedness gives P⊆θ, while stability and leastness give θ⊆P. Deterministic balanced-tree melding and smaller-to-larger member maintenance give O(B+(W+E) log(W+E)) time and O(W+E+B) space without a W·B table. Both outcomes have O(W+E)-size certificates verifiable in O(W+E+B): a negative certificate is any stable partition separating the start from all outer-pin wires, and a positive certificate is a chronological forest of forced folds.

The structural lens yields a second recognizable source-linear family in addition to graded graphs. In the reversed feature graph, topologically compute the canonical longest-path level λ. If, for each box X and tail level s, all corresponding arcs end at one head level, then folds preserve levels. The closure at head level r consequently depends only on already-final lower target classes and is exactly the connected components of stars grouping origins by (X,target class). Topological sorting, the stratification test, all sparse groups, and all stars have total size O(W+E+B). This condition permits non-graded graphs: a direct feature arc may skip a level while a two-arc path has the same endpoints, which contradicts unit-difference grading, yet same-box collisions can still occur and are handled by the level sweep. The earlier graded algorithm remains useful on graded instances not accepted by this canonical-level condition.

Two exact families delimit natural unrestricted attempts. The one-box chain has n+1 changing synchronous rounds with W=2n+3 and E=2n+2, so repeated whole-edge rescanning can be quadratic. For N=2^h, fresh-box rules serialize a balanced bottom-up sequence of data-class unions. Each data wire carries a distinct live Y_i representative whose matching occurrence waits at an anchor. After the balanced root forms, successive anchor and Y_i collisions form a control chain, and only its last equality makes the non-outer start equivalent to an outer wire. Thus the representatives cannot be discarded as globally unique or irrelevant. At every level, either operand of each balanced union contains one live Y-key per data wire, forcing N/2 inspections per level for any implementation that scans a whole operand dictionary. With W=4N+2, E=6N, and B=3N, this is Ω((W+E+B) log(W+E+B)) work in that eager-melding paradigm. It does not preclude a lazy, shared, or otherwise different source-linear algorithm.

The diagnostic warnings were independently checked rather than treated as authority. Least stable closure remains distinct from an arbitrary stable model; the radix argument uses the correct stable-pass invariant; both lower-bound inductions include their boundary cases; and the new level theorem is justified by forcedness plus terminal stability, not by extrapolation from small tests. The unrelated hits do not change the proof. Thus the new decomposition strictly enlarges the proven linear-time territory while leaving the unrestricted open target unsolved.
